chunks: And this Khidr (peace be upon him) is alive since before our time, from the era of Musa (peace be upon him), according to the majority of the Ummah, and until our time, by the consensus of the historians.
No one knows his place of residence, and no one knows if he has any companions, except what the Quran has brought regarding his story with Musa (peace be upon him).

And what some people mention is that he appears at times and is not recognized, and whoever sees him thinks he is one of the ascetics; so when he leaves his place, the one named Khidr is imagined by him, but he did not know him specifically in that moment, nor did he think of him as Khidr specifically, but rather believed that he was one of the people of that time.
ai.seo_question: Who is Khidr and is he still alive according to Shia scholars?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi clarifies that Khidr (a.s.) is a distinct, living figure known to the majority of the Ummah since the time of Musa (a.s.), rather than a symbolic entity or merely a misidentified ascetic. He notes that while his specific location and companions remain unknown, his existence is affirmed by both Quranic narrative and continuous tradition, distinguishing him from the concept of the Hidden Imam’s extraordinary birth. This discussion serves to ground the reality of Khidr’s presence in time, providing a parallel for understanding the nature of the Imam of the Time (a.s.).
